content.content:
Applies to the ten recorded edges, one prerequisite at a time: read the dependent against each prerequisite in depends_on and apply the three criteria to that edge. The evaluation is satisfied only when all ten edges pass.

1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts the prerequisite. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element and the prerequisite it departs from.

2. Edge use: in the dependent, find the element whose soundness this prerequisite carries. Fail naming the prerequisite when the dependent contains no such element; an unused recorded edge is a finding, not a licence.

3. Set coherence, applied to the prerequisites that fix one object between them: the ownership prerequisite fixes what a change owns and from which document it is derived, the stale prerequisite fixes which owned set a landing compares and where that set is read, and the lifecycle prerequisite fixes that a draft has one landing and a landed record no second one. Apply all three to the same object at once, and read the set of paths a landing may place as a union of two sources, neither narrowing the other: the target change's owned set as it currently stands, read at the change that owns the node, together with the ref paths the draft's node document adds. A path a landing places must be owned by the target change either before the recording — in that current owned set — or through the node document the recording writes; no path outside that union is placed. Every changed path of the union is placed by the one landing the draft has: a changed path the union owns may not be left for a recording that a landed record will never allow. A ref path the draft's node document drops stays in the union through the target's current owned set, so the check reads it as an owned and placeable path like any other and adds no rule about how a removal is carried, while content the draft leaves as the target change already holds it is simply unchanged. The set the stale comparison reads does not move with the union: it is the target's current owned set as the stale prerequisite fixes it — not the union, and not the paths a call names. Fail when the dependent's reading leaves a changed path of the union outside the one landing, so the draft can reach its landed end holding content no recording remains able to place; fail, symmetrically, when that reading excludes from the set it may place a path the target change already owns, when it lets a recording place a path the union does not hold, or when it makes the stale comparison read the union or the paths a call names.

Nothing is pre-named: which clause of the dependent is at issue, and against which prerequisite, is what the check discovers at check time, never what the criteria fix in advance.
content.rationale:
All ten recorded prerequisites are inline and so is the dependent, so every edge is read as a written commitment. Nine of the ten are prose and take the natural→natural cell's licence check; zxrrwrky is an EARS requirement sentence — constrained notation — and its edge from a natural dependent falls in the matrix's default cell, which is the same gate form plus a note to extend the matrix. The check is applied once per recorded prerequisite in turn, by reading the recorded documents; a natural-layer child is a commitment in words, not behaviour, so this unit claims no repository path and there is no command to execute.

Criterion 2 exists because this one evaluation carries the coverage of ten recorded edges. An evaluation gates the dependent's use of a prerequisite, not the mere absence of a clash with a prerequisite nothing in the dependent invokes; without the second criterion an edge the dependent never reaches would pass vacuously. Which element fails, and against which prerequisite, is the check's output, not part of any criterion. Criteria 1 and 2 are applied edge by edge; criterion 3 is the one test that spans edges, and it is stated in terms of the object the prerequisites share so that it stays independent of the dependent's wording.

What each edge carries into the check. The registry parent fixes where a record is and how it is found: one JSON document per record at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, the filename the handle, no part of a record kept anywhere else, the records found by scanning that directory, and a landed record retained rather than deleted. The record the source names is reached as that one document, and the landing's state update is written into that same document; a landing that found the record through an index beside the documents, or that removed the document when the draft landed, departs from this parent.

The stale parent fixes what the landing compares: a content-identity base of the node's owned set written at opening, compared path by path against the owned set as it stands at landing, with a stale draft refusing the recording, naming the differing paths, and placing nothing. The dependent's landing is that recording, so a landing that skipped the comparison, or that placed an edit and refused afterwards, departs from this parent.

The record parent fixes the record's identity and references: the handle alone is the key, the node, the edit and the workspace are references, a record names exactly one node, and a record is not a node document. So the source addresses a draft by its handle, the record's target node is the node a landing must agree with — which is what makes a `--to` naming another node refusable — and a landing writes no `nodes/` document and attributes nothing to a change.

The lifecycle parent fixes the two states and the one-way transition: `open` is the record of a draft that has not landed, `landed` one that has, only `open`→`landed` occurs, and the landed record is retained. A landing acts on an open draft, turns that record with the draft it records, and keeps it; a landing of an already landed record, or a delete at landing, departs from this parent.

The operation parent fixes that a registry write is not an operation, that landing is the recording it already is, and that the record's `landed` update is partial work inside that recording rather than a second operation beside it. The landing here is one recording; the state update rides inside it and is not bracketed as an operation of its own.

The recording parent fixes the placement form: `record <path>... --to <id>` places the edits into the named node's change, `--to` is required and names that node, no invocation lands an edit outside an owning change, and recording creates no node. The dependent keeps `--to` required, places into the change that node names, and creates nothing; a source form adds how the draft and its edits are selected and adds refusals, not a second verb and not a second landing.

The draft-model parent fixes that a draft names exactly one node and the edit it belongs to, that a node may carry several drafts, that each draft is written in its own workspace, and that landing is per draft. The source therefore names one draft whose record names one node, landing is per record, and the `--to` must be that node.

The ownership parent fixes the owned set: the node document plus the repo-relative paths in `content.ref` when it is an array, the node document alone when it is inline, and nothing else, the set derived from that node document rather than from a tree, a workspace or the paths a call names. The paths a landing records are the changed paths of that union — the owned set the target change holds, together with the ref paths the draft's document adds — and not other paths in the workspace, the change or the working copy.

Criterion 3 exists because the owned set is fixed twice, from two ends, and the dependent's clause on the paths a landing records sits between them. This evaluation covers a refine, and the refined clause is that junction: the ownership parent derives the set from the node document — the document plus the ref paths that document lists — while the stale parent reads that set at the change that owns the node, taken at landing, and the lifecycle parent leaves each draft one landing and a landed record no way back. Read one edge at a time, each of those can be met by a dependent that takes the owned set from a single place at a single moment, and the joint constraint is exactly what an edge-at-a-time criterion cannot see; so a criterion is needed that holds the three against one object. It derives nothing beyond the three, and it takes the landable set as a union of the two sources the recording has: the target change owns, before anything is written, its node document plus the ref paths that document already lists, and the recording then writes the node document the draft carries into that change, which makes owned the ref paths the draft's document adds. Neither source narrows the other. A path the draft's document drops is still owned by the target change, so it stays placeable and the criterion adds no rule about how a removal is carried, while content the draft leaves exactly as the target holds it is unchanged rather than something to place; a path the draft's document adds is owned as soon as the document is written, so its edit belongs to the same recording rather than to a second one. Because the same draft has no second recording, every changed path of that union is placed by that one landing or not at all. Criterion 3 checks that conjunction, and it keeps the stale parent's set where that parent puts it: the comparison reads the target's current owned set as that parent fixes it, not the union and not the paths a call names, and a dependent that widened the comparison to the union, or narrowed it to the paths a call names, would be the symmetric failure. It fixes none of the things the parents leave open — which of the record's references reaches the change, how the content identity is encoded, whether the ownership test is taken once or path by path, in what order the recording writes anything, what a refusal's text and status are, or what a draft may do after a refusal.

The identity parent fixes that a node's id is the id of the jj change that owns it and appears in the filename and edge targets, never as document content. The `--to` names a node by that id, and a refusal of a source that resolves to the target change turns on that same identity rather than on a commit id, a workspace or a record handle.

The empty-object parent fixes the path-only invocation: `deccy record --to <id>` naming no path refuses the invocation and places nothing. That parent is what makes the source form's optional paths a distinct argument surface: paths may be omitted only because a source supplies them, so path-optionality has to be scoped to the source form while `record --to <id>` with no path still refuses; a dependent that made every `record` invocation path-optional would contradict this parent, and criterion 1 would name the element.

Readings taken where the dependent's form pulls against a parent. On zxrrwrky, the parent is read as fixing the invocation that selects edits by path and names none: a source is a different selection surface, not that invocation, so omitting paths together with a source does not contradict it — but the reading does not license omitting them without one, and a dependent that said otherwise would be a contradicting element under criterion 1. On rvyrosmp, `--to` required and placement-only are read as binding the source form too: a source selects the edits, not the destination, and the recording still creates no node. On xwyryumr, the refusal of a source that is the target change is read as comparing the node identity that parent fixes — the owning jj change id — so a comparison resting on a commit id, a workspace or a handle departs from it. None of these readings narrows a criterion: each is a place the recorded parent already decides, and the check discovers whether the dependent kept it.

The check enforces only what the ten recorded prerequisites state and presupposes no decision beyond them: the exact wording, separators, ordering, stream and exit status of a refusal, whether a stale comparison is made eagerly or path by path, the encoding of any content identity, the order in which a recording writes anything, and how a handle is generated are not fixed here. The criteria name the prerequisites' own objects and no element of the dependent, so rewriting the dependent without changing what it decides leaves all three criteria intact.
